changeSummary: Disclose which data the local MCP adapter returns to a connected chat app, what that app may send to its provider, and how PLVS handles the last connected app name and time.
dateRationale: November 25, 2026 is the planned first stable availability of local MCP. A chat app can receive measurement and application data through this new opt-in interface.
scope: Review of desktop data handling from v0.26.4 (7f3565a6) through 85d60a75 plus the 0.27.0 release documentation and policy.

evidence.notes: The adapter exchanges tool requests and results over local standard input and output, using the existing Agent Control connection and commands. Responses can include measurement data, exported documents and screenshots. Audio inputs and generated recordings remain local. A chat app controls what it sends to its own provider.
The chat app name and last-use time are available in Settings from in-memory state. PLVS does not persist this usage status or send it to a remote service.

evidence.source: PLVS: src-tauri/src/update_runtime.rs, src-tauri/vendor/tauri-plugin-updater and release-range review of feedback, crash reports and newsletter paths
evidence.notes: The updater reads the signed Debian entry for Linux dev checks and removes legacy Windows ZIP update support. The existing GitHub feed, consent settings, feedback and crash submission paths, and newsletter service are unchanged.

limitations: Review covers PLVS source and the local MCP interface. Third-party chat apps determine their provider behavior and retention. The unchanged feedback, crash report and newsletter services were not re-audited.
